properties.error_model: `DynoError`. An unknown column family is refused rather than created. NO SILENT FALLBACK: with the `rocksdb` feature off, `open_rocksdb` fails loud instead of quietly returning the in-memory backend, so a caller can never believe it has durability it does not have.
properties.name: KvBackend trait — the byte seam under StorageEngine
properties.operations: Six byte-level primitives over six named column families: get(cf, key) -> Option<bytes>; put(cf, key, value); delete(cf, key); prefix_scan(cf, prefix) -> ordered (key, value) pairs; prefix_delete(cf, prefix); commit_batch(ops) applying Put / Delete / PrefixDelete atomically and IN ORDER.
properties.payload_schema: Opaque bytes on both sides. The seam is deliberately schema-blind: every schema-aware behaviour — validation, the reverse index, the read cache, the write-buffer overlay, the full-text sidecar — sits ABOVE this trait in StorageEngine, and everything that touches bytes goes through it. Keys are built by `foundation/store/keys.rs` and namespaced by graph_id, which is what lets many graphs share one instance.
